topic: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs specification
query: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs specification
title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs | RFC Editor
snippet: RFC 9457 defines a "problem detail" to carry machine-readable details of errors in HTTP response content to avoid the need to define new error response formats for HTTP APIs. This document obsoletes RFC 7807 and defines JSON and XML document formats to describe the specifics of a problem encountered.
claim: RFC 9457 standardizes machine-readable HTTP error responses in JSON and XML formats, obsoleting RFC 7807.

topic: Problem Details JSON structure and application/problem+json media type
title: REST API Error Handling - Problem Details Response
snippet: A Problem Details response uses the application/problem+json content type and includes fields: type (URI identifying the error category), title (short human-readable summary), status (HTTP status code), detail (specific explanation), and instance (URI identifying the specific request). Extensions can add application-specific fields.
claim: RFC 9457 defines a five-field standard (type, title, status, detail, instance) with extensibility for custom fields.

topic: RFC 9457 error type registry for interoperability

title: Welcome to Problem Details Registry.
snippet: RFC 9457 introduces an IANA registry for hosting common problem type URIs. The registry promotes reuse of widely used problem types and requires Specification Required registration for new entries. The standard registers "about:blank" as a problem type indicating no additional semantics beyond the HTTP status code.
claim: RFC 9457 establishes an IANA registry for standardized problem type URIs to enable interoperable error handling.

title: Best Practices for API Error Handling - Zuplo
snippet: Use consistent error responses across your API via RFC 9457. The detail field should help developers fix the problem without contacting support. Include Retry-After on 429 and 503 responses, and return all validation errors at once with field-level detail. RFC 9457 supports custom extension members for application-specific context.
claim: RFC 9457 best practices include consistent error responses, actionable detail fields, and validation-error batching.

title: Building Resilient Microservices Architecture in a Cloud-Native Environment
snippet: Structured error handling includes implementing circuit breakers, request timeouts, idempotent APIs, and bulkheads. Structured logging with trace IDs correlates logs with traces; structured logs should be in JSON format and include correlation IDs for error tracking.
